newsitem.title: USA: Delta Air names acting CEO, chairman.
newsitem.headline: Delta Air names acting CEO, chairman.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc. said Thursday it named two acting officers to head the nation's third-largest carrier after Chairman Ronald Allen retires at the end of the month.

Delta said Mary Johnston Evans, a member of Delta's board since 1983, will serve as acting non-executive chairman, and Maurice Worth has been named acting chief executive officer. Worth is currently the airline's executive vice president of customer service and acting chief operating officer.
Worth was named acting COO in May when Allen announced his retirement.
Allen's departure after 34 years with Delta surprised industry experts, who suggested at the time that his resignation followed a rift with the board about the company's strategic focus.
Delta said Worth will oversee the airline's daily worldwide operations, while Evans will handle board issues until a permanent chairman is named.

"The entire board of directors feels a real sense of urgency about finding a new leader for Delta, but we don't feel rushed. We intend to find the very best person to lead Delta Air Lines. There is no self-imposed deadline," Evans said.
Worth, a 36-year veteran at Delta, said he was not a candidate for the job of permanent CEO.
"I have not been interviewed for the job and I am doing the job that I have been assigned to do," Worth said.

"I've been part of the vision and part of the strategy and I have been asked to continue to take the company forward during this transition period and I'm concentrating my efforts on that," Worth said.
Once Delta names a permanent chief executive, Worth said he hopes to play "an active roll at Delta."
"I've committed 36 years to the company and have been a part of the success and part of the Delta people. I hope I can take an active roll going forward."
During his career at Delta, Worth has worked in operations, station management, personnel and executive management.
The company declined to comment on the time frame for its executive search or to discuss how many candidates have been interviewed.

At a press conference in Atlanta, Evans said the company is looking at candidates both inside and outside the airline industry. Evans has served on a number of corporate boards, including Baxter International Inc., Dun & Bradstreet Corp. and Household International Inc.
Delta stock rose 31 cents to $88.50 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
